## tsa06-p01
It is stated by the word station-placing. Therein station is threefold: breath-wind, body, and outer. Therein in breath, for now, the whole course to be stated: the course, breath-located, is imagined. Of it, successive-nonsuccessive-grasping alone is time; and it is the Lord himself shining within. And its shining of God is power named Time; but differenced, that shining of succession-nonsuccession is breath-function. (6.1) For consciousness itself, taking divided form from knowables — hence therefore, through limitation-yoga, going to knowableness, is void. Then through autonomy, falling with eagerness to appropriate in the knowable, action-power-chief, breathing-natured, life-natured, since filling body by five forms, hence it shines as if conscious. (6.2) Therein in action-power is the time-course in the eastern part; but in the northern is the place-course of body-variety-nature. Therein of letter-mantra-word-courses the standing is in the time-course, through gross-subtle-supreme-nature. (6.3) But of place-course standing, as principle-person-śakti-natured — so it will be in its place. (6.4) Therein, though in body breath is warp-woof-formed with outer-inner, nevertheless it whose effort is clearly felt is from heart onward — hence thence itself it is to be expounded. (6.5) Therein lord-power, self-power, effort — the triad is the cause in breath-impelling, through quality-chief-nature. (6.6) Therein from heart to twelve-end-end, by own fingers, of all is thirty-six fingers of breath-course, in exit and in entry, through own-fitting-power-effort-body-nature of all. (6.7) Therein water-hour, lunar day, month, and year, year-mass-natured — thus entire time is completed. Therein in one-and-quarter finger is a drop-moment: thus standing is water-hour-rise; for the water-hour is by sixty drops; hence it is seventy-two fingers. (6.8) Now lunar-day-rise. (6.9) Two fingers plus quarter is called instant; in four of them is a watch; half-instant-half therein is junction itself; thus in exit is day, in entry night — thus is lunar-day-rise. (6.10) Now month-rise. (6.11) Therein day is dark fortnight, night is bright; therein the former half-instant and latter half-instant are rest, untimed; the middle fifteen instants alone are lunar days; therein manifestation and rest — these alone are day-nights. (6.12) Therein knowableness-madeness-manifestation is day; of knowable, dissolution in the considerer is night; and they, manifestation-and-rest, through long-short-variety are of endless division; in their equality is equinox. (6.13) Therein in dark fortnight the breath-sun offers to the down-breath-moon one by one a digit — until at fifteenth instant the moon, with wasted separate-spread digits, near twelve-end dissolves in breath-sun itself. (6.14) Right after that, whatever half-instant is fortnight-joint. (6.15) Of it, of the half-instant, the former half is new-moon, the second is first-day. (6.16) Therein on first day, in that part, when that new-moon part, through sneeze-effort-attention-made day-division, enters — then therein is seizing. Therein, with knowable-formed-moon, the Māyā-knower-Rāhu, by nature unable to dissolve, merely covering-capable, drinks the sun-dwelling lunar nectar — hence. (6.17)

## tsa06-p01 — where time lives
"Station" is the word: three of them — breath, body, outside. The whole course sits in breath, and time just is grasping in sequence and out of it — the Lord shining inside, whose shining is goddess Time; differenced, it's breath doing its work. How breath starts: awareness takes a divided shape from knowables and goes void with limitation; then, free, it drops into some knowable wanting to own it — mostly action — breathes, lives, fills the body five ways, and looks conscious. Time's course runs east in action-power; place's runs north in body's variety (letters, mantras, words stand in time's course, gross to supreme; place's course — principles, persons, powers — in its own place later). Breath weaves in and out of the body, but the felt push starts at the heart — so start there. Three drive it: lord-power, self-power, effort, chief by turns. Measure: heart to twelve-end, thirty-six fingers out and back. Water-hour, day, month, year, year-masses — time complete. A finger and a quarter is a drop; sixty drops an hour of seventy-two fingers. Two fingers and a quarter, an instant; four instants, a watch; half-instants the joints — breathing out is day, breathing in is night: that's the lunar day. The month: out-breath's fortnight is "day," in-breath's is "night"; the joints at the ends rest outside time; fifteen instants between are the days — showing is day, resting is night. Showing-of-the-known is day; its melting into the knower is night; long and short run endless, equal is equinox. In the dark half the breath-sun feeds the down-breath moon digit by digit till, at the fifteenth, the thinned moon melts near the twelve-end into the sun. Next half-instant: the joint — new moon's half, first day's half. When a sneeze-cut lets the new-moon slice into the first day, that's eclipse: Māyā's knower-Rāhu can't unmake anything, only cover — so he drinks the moon's nectar where it sits in the sun.
*Fidelity: preserved (stations, breath-genesis, east/north, heart-start, full measure table, fortnight, eclipse). Added: none doctrinal. Not-resolved: measures throughout (REALIA).*

The passage moves in eight steps. (1) Three stations + breath-located course + succession-grasping = time = Lord within (Kālī). (2) Breath-genesis: consciousness takes divided form from knowables → void → free → drops into knowable → action-breath → life → five forms fill body → as-if conscious. (3) Time-course east (action), place-course north (body-variety); letter-mantra-word in time-course (gross→supreme); place-course (principles/persons/powers) deferred. (4) Felt-effort at heart → expound from heart; three causes (lord-power, self-power, effort). (5) Full measure table (36 fingers each way; ghaṭikā/tithi/māsa/varṣa; 1.25 finger = caṣaka; 60 = ghaṭikā = 72 fingers; tuṭi/prahara/junction). (6) Month-rise: dark=day, bright=night; end-rests timeless; 15 middle tuṭis; manifestation/rest = day/night; knowable-manifestation = day, dissolution-in-considerer = night; endless division; equality = equinox. (7) Dark fortnight: breath-sun offers digits to apāna-moon until 15th tuṭi moon dissolves in breath-sun; next half-tuṭi = joint (new-moon half + first-day half). (8) First-day sneeze-cut entry = eclipse: Māyā-knower-Rāhu covers (can't dissolve), drinks solar lunar nectar.

## tsa06-p02
Through non-division-making of knower-means-known-triad, it is holy time, otherworld-fruit-giving. (6.18) Then entering in breath, consciousness-sun fills down-breath-moon digit by digit — until fifteenth instant is full moon; right after that fortnight-joint and seizing as before; but that is this-world-fruit-giving — thus is month-rise. (6.19) Now year-rise. (6.20) Therein in dark fortnight itself is northern course: in six-six fingers is transit, from Capricorn to Gemini-end. (6.21) Therein per finger are five lunar days; there too day-night-division; thus in entry is southern course: embryo-ness, rise-wish, about-to-rise-ness, futurity, rise-beginning, risen-ness, and birth-and-rest six changes — thus in order in Capricorn and the rest. (6.22) Likewise worship here makes fitting fruit. (6.23) Here too Dakṣa-to-Grandfather Rudras and powers, twelve lords — thus is year-rise. (6.24) Per finger are sixty lunar days — thus in order: at transit is a year. By this course of exit-entry is twelve-year rise; per finger three hundred lunar days; in one-and-quarter finger is a year — where before the drop was stated. By counting, at transit five years. By this series, in one breath-exit-entry-time is sixty-year rise; here twenty-one thousand six hundred is the tithi number. (6.25) So many alone in day-night is breath-number — hence beyond sixty-year rise is not examined, from infinity. (6.26) Therein human year is gods' day; by this course twelve thousand divine years is an eon. (6.27) Four, three, two, one — from kṛta onward, by so many hundreds are eight joints. (6.28) By seventy-one eons is a Manu-age; by fourteen Manu-ages is Brahmā's day. At Brahmā-day-end, in the fire-burnt triple world and in the other smoke-veiled triple world, all folk, fire-driven swiftly, in Jana world becoming dissolute abide. (6.29) But the awake — Kūṣmāṇḍa, Hāṭakeśa and the rest — sport in the Great world. (6.30) Then at night's completion is Brahmī creation. (6.31) By this measure a hundred years is Brahmā's life. (6.32) That is Viṣṇu's day and so long his night; his too a hundred is life. (6.33) That day, above it, of Rudra-world-lord Rudra is so long night; as before, a year, and that hundred too is the limit. (6.34) Therein at Rudra's end is going to Śiva-hood; Rudra's stated-tenure-limit; of universe-bearers that day is a hundred Rudras' night, so long; theirs too a hundred is life. (6.35) At hundred-Rudra-expiry is universe-destruction. (6.36) Thus from water-principle to unmanifest-end, this same in course is Rudras' life. (6.37) The prior's life is the latter's day. (6.38) Thence Brahmā and Rudras, non-transgressing officers, abide in the unmanifest. (6.39) And Śrīkaṇṭha then is the withdrawer. (6.40) This is interim dissolution; at its expiry, creation. (6.41) Therein other-śāstra-taught too are created. (6.42) But what is Śrīkaṇṭha's own life, that is kañcuka-Rudras' day, so long night; what is their life, that is Gahaneśa's day, so long night; and therein everything dissolves in Māyā. (6.43)"

## tsa06-p02 — up the ladder of ages
Why eclipses count: knower, knowing, known undivided — holy time, fruit beyond. Run the month backward — breath filling moon to full — and the fruit is here-and-now. The year: dark half is the northward run, a transit every six fingers from Capricorn to Gemini, five days a finger with days and nights; the inward run is southward — conception, will-to-rise, almost-risen, to-come, starting, risen, birth and five more changes, sign by sign. Worship tunes the fruit. Twelve lords — Rudras Dakṣa to Grandfather, and powers — own the year. Sixty days a finger makes a year a transit; out-and-in makes twelve years; three hundred a finger; a year and a quarter-finger (drops, as before); five years a transit by the count; one full out-and-in breath, sixty years — 21,600 day-beats, the breaths of a day and night. Past sixty years don't ask: it's endless. A human year is a gods' day; twelve thousand of those, an eon (four-three-two-one, eight joints); seventy-one eons a Manu-age; fourteen, Brahmā's day. At his day's end the triple world burns, the other smokes, beings herd dazed into the world of Jana and wait out dissolution — while the awake, Kūṣmāṇḍa and the lords of gold, play on in the Great world. Night ends, Brahmā creates. A hundred such years is his life — a day of Viṣṇu, and his night as long, his life a hundred too; that, a day above for Rudra lord of Rudra's world, his night as long, his bound a hundred too. At Rudra's end, Śiva-hood; his tenure stated. The bearers' day is a hundred Rudras' night, and as long; their life a hundred; at a hundred Rudras gone, the egg breaks. So from water to unmanifest for the Rudras, each life the next one's day. Brahmā and the Rudras, holding office clean, sit out in the unmanifest — and Śrīkaṇṭha draws it all in. That's the lesser ending; then creating again (other books' gods too).
*Fidelity: preserved (merit rule, year machinery, 12 lords, full age-ladder to interim dissolution). Added: "the egg breaks" for brahmāṇḍavināśa (register). Not-resolved: Purāṇic furniture (external).*

So from water to unmanifest for the Rudras, each life the next one's day. Brahmā and the Rudras, holding office clean, sit out in the unmanifest — and Śrīkaṇṭha draws it all in. That's the lesser ending; then creating again (other books' gods too).

The passage has two movements. First, merit and month/year: eclipse holy (triad undivided) → otherworld fruit; reverse month → this-world fruit; year machinery (north/south course, 12 lords, 60/300/1.25-finger counts, 21,600 breaths). Second, cosmic ages: 60-year rise stops (infinity); human year = gods' day; eon/Manu-age/Brahmā day with dissolution tableau (Jana world, Mahas sport, recreation); Brahmā/Viṣṇu/Rudra/Śiva tenure ladder; 100-Rudra expiry = destruction; water-to-unmanifest law; officers abide; Śrīkaṇṭha withdraws = interim dissolution.

"[P3 covers 6.44–6.70: Gahaneśa recreates; unmanifest-time ×10 parārdhas = Māyā day/night = dissolution; Māyā-time ×100 parārdhas = Īśvara day (breath creates world; night breath-calm; order even in calm consciousness); Īśvara-time ×100 parārdhas = Sadāśiva day/night = great dissolution (Sadāśiva crosses bindu/half-moon/obstruction into sound→power→pervader→unsupported); power-time × crores of parārdhas = unsupported day; unsupported in mindless station = equilibrium = Brahman. (6.44–6.52) From equilibrium timelessness flashes the whole time-spread-dissolution-wheel; one-ten-hundred-thousand…×10 to eighteen is the counting rule. (6.53–6.54) Countless creations-dissolutions in one great-creation breath; breath in consciousness, consciousness in condition, condition in mere consciousness — this throb named time-rise. Hence dream-resolve variety is uncontradicted. (6.55–6.56) So as breath's time-rise, so apāna's too, heart to root-seat; as at heart-throat-palate-brow-randhra-twelve-end the six causes Brahmā-Viṣṇu-Rudra-Lord-Sadāśiva-Unsupported, so in apāna too at heart-bulb-joy-contraction-expansion-twelve-end: childhood-youth-age-death-rebirth-liberation lords. (6.57–6.58) Now samāna's time-rise. Samāna, moving in ten heart-channels, drives sap and the rest evenly through the whole body. (6.59) Moving in the eight directions, it mimics the direction-lords' play for the knower. (6.60) Moving up-down, it goes-comes in three channels. (6.61) Therein on equinox day, outside at dawn, it carries one-and-quarter water-hours in the middle course. (6.62) Then nine hundred breath-distractions — by counting, outside two-and-half water-hours, left-right-left-right-left: five transits. (6.63) Past the five-transit, in thirteen-and-three-quarter elapsed water-hours, south autumn equinox-noon: nine hundred breaths. (6.64) Thence too right-left-right-left-right: transit-five of nine-hundreds each — thus even at night. (6.65) Thus on equinox day and its night, twelve-twelve transits. (6.66) Then with day-growth-decay, transit-growth-decay. (6.67) Thus in one samāna-breath is two years, from breath-in-out-yoga-absence. (6.68) Here too twelve-year-rise and the rest as before. (6.69–6.70)]"

## tsa06-p03 — past Māyā, and the other breaths (CONDENSED companion to L1)
Gahaneśa rebuilds. Multiply unmanifest time by ten vastnesses: a day of Māyā, and as long a night — that is dissolution. Multiply Māyā-time by a hundred: a day of the Lord — breath builds the world, night stills the breath, and even in the stillness the order holds, since awareness keeps its sequence. Multiply again by a hundred: Sadāśiva's day and night — the great ending, where he climbs past point, half-moon, and blockage into sound, into power, into the pervader, into the Unsupported. Multiply power-time by crores of vastnesses: the Unsupported's day; and the Unsupported, stationed past mind, is poise — is Brahman. Out of that poise, timeless, spins the whole wheel of time spreading and melting: one, ten, a hundred, a thousand, up eighteen ranks of ten — that is counting. Creations and dissolutions past number fit in one great breath; breath sits in awareness, awareness in its condition, condition in bare awareness — and that throb is what "time rising" means. So dreams can differ without breaking anything. Apāna keeps the same time from heart to root-seat, with its six causes and its lords of childhood to freedom. Samāna runs ten heart-channels feeding the body's saps, aping the eight direction-lords, climbing three channels up and down — dawn measures and nine-hundred counts all accounted, twelve transits by day and twelve by night, growing with the days; one samāna-breath is two years, no in-and-out needed.

## tsa06-p04
"In udāna the course to twelve-end is of throb-only time; here too the course as before. (6.71) But in pervading, through all-pervadingness, though sequenceless, by subtle upsurge-yoga is time-rise. (6.72) Now letter-rise. Therein every half-watch is class-rise; at equinox even: of letter upon letter, two hundred sixteen breaths outside and thirty-six drops — thus the rise; this effortless letter-rise. (6.73–6.74) But effort-born is mantra-rise: like Persian-wheel-machine-carrying, by single-link power, marvelous, mantra-rise day-night reflecting, one reaches identity with mantra-god. (6.75) Therein, by ever-risen breath-course-number itself is rise-number explained; doubled, halved and so on in course: in hundred-eight-wheel two hundred rises — thus in course, in gross-subtle course-nature-rested, with thinned breath-course, when time-grasp is done, complete one consciousness, marvel-power-full, shines. (6.76) Time-difference alone divides consciousness, not knowable-difference — like peak-standing-knowledge; of knowledge, as long as its abiding-time, that alone is instant; and in one breath-rise necessarily one knowledge alone — else there would be no sequential word-tainted thought-unit at all, since mora too is sequential — as it was said: 'of it, from ta, high, half-short.' (6.77–6.78) Hence until another throb rises, there is one knowledge alone. (6.79) Hence therefore at eighty-one-word-recall-time, through varied-nature-entry, that one Lord-directed thought, in time-grasp, becomes thought-free itself. (6.80) Thus seeing the entire time-course in breath-rise itself, and the varied countless creations-dissolutions therein, reckoning there, recognizing own Lordhood itself, one is freed indeed. (6.81–6.82)"

## tsa06-p04 — letters, mantra, and what seeing time does
Udāna runs to the twelve-end on throbbing time alone; the all-breath, everywhere, rises time by subtle upsurge without sequence. Letters rise every half-watch by classes — at equinox evenly: 216 breaths a letter outside, 36 drops — effortless letter-rise. Mantra-rise takes work: like a water-wheel's chain, one link pulling, it turns day and night reflecting, wonderfully, till you are the mantra's god. The ever-risen breath-count is the rise-count — doubled, halved, and so on: two hundred rises in the 108-wheel; rest in gross-and-subtle course-nature, thin the breath-course, finish grasping time, and one whole awareness shines, full of marvel-power. Only time's difference divides awareness — never the thing's (like knowledge on a peak: a knowing lasts exactly its abiding, and that is an instant). One breath-rise, one knowing, necessarily — else no word-wearing thought-whole could sequence at all, mora being sequential too ("of it: high from ta, half-short"). Till the next throb, one knowing stands. So at eighty-one words recalled, through every kind of entry, the one Lord-aimed thought turns thought-free itself inside time's grasp. Seeing the whole time-course in breath's rise, with its countless makings and unmakings reckoned there, knowing your own Lordhood — you are free. Indeed.
